ideas.title: Clap, and the island answers (playable)
ideas.nearest: The island answers a clap, a broken take
ideas.critique: This is the failed clap take done properly. It adds things that take lacked: a key the player presses, a lit wavefront in arrival order, and creatures timed to real ray arrivals, with occluded friends answering later. Those are real steps beyond a soundtrack heard from a fixed spot. The risk is the same as last time: if the ring and the head turns don't read on screen, it repeats the broken take, and hide and seek is promised but has no scoring yet.

ideas.title: Fireflies that learn your rhythm
ideas.critique: Mirollo-Strogatz pulse coupling on the GPU is an emergent simulation the island has never had. Watching scattered sparks fall into one field-wide wave that you led is the kind of thing people clip. Its weak spot is the play: if the lantern rhythm is only a key held down at any tempo, the teaching is shallow.

ideas.title: The owl that hears you
ideas.nearest: The island answers a clap, a broken take
ideas.critique: Stealth by traced sound, with loudness set by the ground's material and by what stands between you and the owl, is a real game mechanic with a clear goal. A new generated creature is the expected part. The binaural time and level estimate is easy to fake with a distance check, and if it is faked the shapes of the world stop mattering.

ideas.title: Lumi folds its wings
ideas.critique: Secondary motion from springs and a T-pose fixed are overdue work on goal 6 and goal 5's self, but they are refinements a viewer expects, not a surprise. Mood-picked idles are scripted clips on top of a spring layer, and nothing about them is playable.

ideas.title: A raft you load like a puzzle
ideas.critique: Buoyancy from the submerged volume with IPC rigid bodies is real physics, and the stacking puzzle has a clear win and loss. The tilt-and-flood payoff with load balance echoes the seesaw island and Keep the island level, which blunts the surprise. Water flooding over the edge without Maelstrom coupling may be only a look.

ideas.title: The island's coin
ideas.critique: Euler's disk spin-down and silver in macro shots are a nice showcase for the tracer, and the strike depth is honest physics. Relief as a height field scaled by the blow is a simple displacement, and handing a coin to a friend is one more prop to keep, fun once.

ideas.title: Rocks that ring
ideas.nearest: The island answers a clap, a broken take
ideas.critique: Pitch from FEM eigenmodes of each rock's real mesh is a genuine engineered system, and showing the mode shape as a shimmer is something no game does. Finding a tune is a thin goal, and the result could be only a quirky xylophone people play once.

ideas.title: Stars to sail by
ideas.critique: A real catalogue turning by sidereal time and stars reflected in the sea is good rendering, but a night sky is an expected item on the rendering goal. The navigation game of pointing at a star is a thin scripted wrapper around it.

ideas.title: Sand that blows
ideas.critique: Werner's slab model with angle-of-repose avalanches is a real step beyond the speech-sand dunes and sand sledding, but sand dunes reshaping the island is a payoff the island has already shown twice. Footprints that fill in and sand piling behind a wall give a little play; the time lapse looks like the earlier dune films.

ideas.title: Camera obscura, sharp
ideas.critique: A designed lens and higher sample counts make the existing hut optically correct, but what a viewer gets is the same upside-down still again, a bit sharper. Walking inside is nice once; the step adds accuracy, not a new thing.
